title: Add KMS metrics + tracing spans for standardized wrapper calls
author: Nadia Rahman
description: Summary: Instruments all KMS operations invoked via the new shared wrapper with metrics and trace spans following Redwood telemetry conventions. Adds latency histograms, request/error counters (tagged by canonical error taxonomy), and a consistent tracing span shape so on-call can correlate KMS degradation to elevated 5xx/latency. Motivation: As we harden KMS integration paths (ENG-4821), we need consistent KMS dependency signals across control-plane and data-plane components. Recent support cases and a throttling-related incident (SUP-19377) showed we lacked enough granularity to quickly answer: (1) which operation is failing, (2) whether it’s retry amplification, (3) what error class dominates, and (4) which region/provider is impacted. This PR builds on pr-18421’s wrapper API and wires metrics/spans at the wrapper boundary (single place, consistent tags). What’s included: Metrics (emitted on every wrapper call): 1) redwood.kms.request.count (counter) tags: operation, provider, region, result (success|error), error_category (when error). 2) redwood.kms.request.latency_ms (histogram) tags: operation, provider, region, result. 3) redwood.kms.retries.count (counter) tags: operation, provider, region, error_category. 4) redwood.kms.throttled.count (counter) tags: provider, region (incremented for throttling-class responses, including SDK-specific throttle codes mapped into the canonical taxonomy). Tracing: Adds a span around each KMS wrapper call: span name: kms.<operation> (e.g., kms.decrypt, kms.encrypt, kms.generate_data_key, kms.describe_key) attributes: kms.operation, kms.provider, cloud.region, kms.key_ref (redacted; alias name when present, otherwise stable hash), kms.retry_attempt (per attempt), kms.error_category (when error), kms.http_status (when available from SDK metadata), and kms.request_id (when provided by provider SDK). Notes: we explicitly do not attach raw key ARNs or plaintext key IDs; key references are sanitized. Error taxonomy mapping: Uses the canonical categories discussed in ENG-4822 and the eng-security thread (AccessDenied, NotFound, Throttling, Timeout, InvalidCiphertext, DependencyUnavailable, Unknown). Mapping is implemented in kms/telemetry/error_mapping.go and shared by metrics + span attributes + logs. Sampling: Spans respect existing tracing sampling decisions (no new always-on sampling); metrics are always emitted. This is intentional so we can alert on dependency health even when traces are sampled. Changed areas (high level): - pkg/security/kms/wrapper/*: inject TelemetryReporter into wrapper client; emit metrics + spans; ensure metrics are recorded for success/failure and for each attempt where relevant. - pkg/telemetry/metrics/registry.go: registers KMS meters and canonical tag keys (prevents ad-hoc tag drift). - pkg/telemetry/tracing/spans.go: helper to build KMS spans with consistent attribute names and safe key redaction. - pkg/security/kms/providers/aws.go, gcp.go, azure.go: normalizes provider-specific error codes into canonical error categories; plumbs request-id and status metadata when available. - docs/internal/observability/metrics.md: adds KMS metric names + tag glossary (internal only). Example metric/tag conventions (for reviewers): - operation values: decrypt | encrypt | generate_data_key | describe_key | reencrypt - provider values: aws | gcp | azure - error_category values: AccessDenied | NotFound | Throttling | Timeout | InvalidCiphertext | DependencyUnavailable | Unknown - region values: us-east-1, etc. (or provider equivalent) Testing: - Unit tests for error mapping across providers (golden table tests). - Unit tests verifying tag sets (ensures we don’t regress into high-cardinality tags). - Local smoke: ran data-plane integration tests against the KMS stub; verified metrics emission via in-process exporter. Rollout / follow-ups: - SRE will add dashboards/alerts in a separate PR (observability-pack/pr-844). - Once wrapper migration is complete across remaining call sites, we can remove legacy ad-hoc KMS logging in services. Checklist: - [x] No sensitive data in metrics/tags (no key ARNs, no account IDs) - [x] Error taxonomy matches ENG-4822 - [x] Metrics follow Redwood naming + tagging conventions - [x] Traces use consistent span naming/attributes - [x] Unit tests for mapping and tag set validation

kms: emit request counters + latency histograms at wrapper boundary

tracing: add kms.<operation> spans with safe attributes
tests: golden mapping + tag set validation
